newsitem.title: USA: Founders Asset Management seeks buyer - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Founders Asset Management seeks buyer - Barron's.

text.p: Founders Asset Management in Denver, Colo. has hired investment banking firm Putman Lovell & Thornton to find a buyer, Barron's investor weekly newspaper reported in its May 26 edition.
Accoring to people familiar with the situation, it could sell for as much as $150 million to $200 million, the newspaper said.

A Founders spokesman was quoted in the newspaper as saying: "It's not hard to imagine people would be interested in the company." But he was quoted as declining to comment on the plans of Founders' chairman and largest shareholder Bjorn Erik Borgen.
Barron's also said Portland-based Crabbe Huson Group hired Goldman Sachs to sell off part of its mutual fund operations, which could fetch over $10 million.
James Crabbe, president of the group, was quoted as saying: "We've asked Goldman Sachs what kind of distribution alternatives are available for our mutual funds."
Barron's said Crabbe was considering selling part of the fund's operation but did not plan to surrender control of the company.
